title: docs(search): name the empty-search-set refusal on the pages that describe the data read route's search
body:
Fixes #24355

Clause-②: no

## What

This PR adds the empty-search-set refusal to every hand-written page that describes the data read route's `search` and did not mention it yet. Since `ec749fbb44` (PR #24320), a non-blank `search` over an object whose search set comes out empty is refused with `400 INVALID_FIELD` instead of answering every row. Until now these pages described field resolution only.

| page | where | change |
|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` | `INVALID_FIELD`, the read-axis parenthesis in the catalog pointer | `search` added beside `searchFields` |
| `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx` | `GET /data/:object` parameter table, `search` row | one sentence: when the set is empty, a non-blank term is `400 INVALID_FIELD`, never every row |
| same | the request/result table under "Neither is a search narrowing, a grouping, or an aggregation" | one row: `?search=alpha` on an object with no searchable field gives `400 INVALID_FIELD` |
| same | the `searchFields` bullet under that table | now names both `search` and `searchFields`. The bullet called `searchFields` "the only parameter whose failure changed which rows came back", and the new row would make that untrue. One sentence says what a bare `search` used to do |
| `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx` | Full-Text Search, opening paragraph | one sentence, engine calls included |
| `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` | field-resolution paragraph | the sentence about internal callers keeping the tolerant intersection now also says what they do not keep: the engine itself refuses on `find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate` (`param: 'search'`) |
| `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx` | Global search | outside the card's four (see Enumeration). One sentence: list search is refused, global search skips the object, mirror the title |
| `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` | Toolbar search runtime table | outside the card's four. The runtime cell of the "key omitted" row gains "`400 INVALID_FIELD` when that set is empty" |

No new section. `content/docs/references/**`, `content/docs/releases/**` and `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` are untouched.

## The producer, read from the code (base `e4bcced0b4`)

- `emptySearchSetError` and its single call site, `ObjectQL.expandSearchOnAst` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`). It throws when the term is non-blank (`normalizeSearch(raw).query.trim()`) and `expandSearchToFilter` returned `null`. The thrown error carries `status`/`httpStatus` 400, `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`, `object` and `param: 'search'`. It has no `field`.
- The set comes from `resolveSearchFieldResolution` (`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`). A declared entry counts when it names a field that exists and is not virtual (`formula`). If no entry counts, the auto-default applies: text / email / phone / url / autonumber / textarea / markdown / select, minus hidden and system columns. `internal: true` fields are removed from the map before resolution.
- Verbs: `find` and `findOne` call `expandSearchOnAst` directly; `count` and `aggregate` reach it through `expandSearchOnOptions`. All four live in the engine, so a caller of `engine.find()` meets the refusal too. That is why query-syntax's sentence about internal callers keeping the tolerant intersection is kept and narrowed, not deleted: the tolerant half, `resolveSearchFields` dropping unknown requested names, has not changed.
- One door still answers `200`. Global search (`searchAll`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) skips an object whose set is empty before it queries. That is stated on schema-design, the only page here that describes global search.
- The REST pages say `400 INVALID_FIELD` and leave out `param`. The flat `/data` arm (the `INVALID_FIELD` arm in `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts`) sends `error`, `code`, `field` and `object`, not `param`. Only query-syntax, which describes the engine's thrown error, names `param: 'search'`.

Sister sentence: the `### INVALID_FIELD` sentence that PR #24353 adds to `error-catalog.mdx`, read at its head `d87f5a77ff`. Each page reuses its terms: resolved search set is empty, no `searchableFields` entry names a stored field, the default search scans none, `internal: true` fields never count, mirror the composed title onto a stored text field. The error-handling parenthesis says the catalog entry lists `search`. That is only true once #24353 lands, so the two should land together or #24353 first.

## Enumeration

`git grep -lE 'searchableFields|searchFields' e4bcced0b4 -- content/docs`, minus `references/` and `releases/`, gives 8 pages. I read each once.

| page | describes the data read route's `search`? | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `api/data-api.mdx` | yes | edited |
| `data-modeling/queries.mdx` | yes | edited |
| `protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` | yes (the `INVALID_FIELD` read axes) | edited |
| `protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` | yes | edited |
| `data-modeling/schema-design.mdx` | yes: `?search=apollo`, `$search`, the auto-default fallback | edited (outside the card's four) |
| `ui/views.mdx` | yes: the toolbar search's runtime answers are the data door's | edited (outside the card's four) |
| `api/error-catalog.mdx` | yes | left: PR #24353 covers it |
| `kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` | no: the `EngineQueryOptions` type listing and the predicate rule for `findOne`, neither of which describes the route | read and left |

## Line budget

The card's four pages: +16 / -6, net +10 (budget +16). The two outside them: schema-design +4 / -1, views +1 / -1. All six: +21 / -8.

## Verification (HEAD `d0e954f51`, after merging `origin/main` at `d1f082d94`)

Docs-only: no package is touched, so no build closure and no package tests are owed. The gate list is the 41 commands from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (merge base `d1f082d94`). Each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe:

- 40 exited 0. They include `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `check:doc-anchors`, `check:error-status-conformance`, `check:nul-bytes` and `check:corpus-claim-drift`. Four of them ran after building `@objectstack/lint...` (lint, formula, sdui-parser, spec) under the verify lock (held 117 s): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:docs`, `pnpm check:docs-transcript-drift`, and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` / `check:doc-security-posture`.
- 1 NOT MEASURED: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because `packages/client-react/dist` holds no `.d.ts`. Building it means a 37-package closure. Declared narrowing: none of the eight hunks is inside a fenced code block (checked per hunk), so no marked example changed. CI runs the gate.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "41 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 40 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED".
- Left to CI, not run locally: the path-scheduled `Build Docs` job and the type-check lanes.
- Control-byte scan of the six files: no hit.

## Acceptance notes

- `ui/views.mdx`, under "What the object allows": the allowed set for a declaring object is described as "that list, verbatim — whatever the field types are". In the code, `resolveSearchFieldResolution` drops entries that name no field or a `formula` field. The last table row in the same section does refuse the formula case. Docs drift, not filed, no carrier.
- `kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`: the `EngineQueryOptions` comment for `search` does not mention the refusal. The engine-caller statement is on query-syntax. Read and left (see above).
